Pumpkin Mochi Hand Pie Recipe

by Mochi Mommy on September 22, 2026
Jump to Recipe
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 6:15
Instaread

Inspired by McDonald’s Japan daifuku pies, this is a pumpkin version perfect for fall. This is a great baking activity with kids as it can use all premade materials like store-bought pie crust and store-bought pumpkin butter. Click jump to recipe to get started or read through the blog post for recipe tips and ingredient information.

What Are Mochi Hand Pies?

We all know that McDonald’s changes their menu to adapt to regional specialties, but some of my absolute favorite are the Japan-specific menu items. I was lucky enough to be in Tokyo in spring when they sell an ichigo daifuku pie. It’s a Japanese version of the classic American McDonald’s apple pie, but with a strawberry mochi filling. Obviously, AMAZING.

Anyway, I was so inspired by the daifuku pie that I tried to adapt it for an easy home-baked recipe. And of course, pie-baking always makes me think of fall so why not turn this into a pumpkin mochi pie? This is great for beginner bakers or baking with kids, as you can use premade pie crust and pumpkin butter from the grocery store.

Ingredient Substitutions and Tips

The pie is made up of four components: a microwave mochi filling, pie crust, pumpkin butter, and an icing on top.

Microwave Mochi

The mochi filling is just a version of my microwave milk mochi recipe. You mix mochiko, sugar, and milk together and microwave it until it becomes a gooey, stretchy mochi. So easy. Generally, I do not recommend substituting other rice flours for the mochiko, as it changes the texture. The only flour substitutes that I recommend is either tapioca starch or shiratamako, but mochiko really is the best for this situation. You can find mochiko in the international aisle of many American grocery stores or buy (at a premium) online.

You can increase or decrease the sugar as needed or try substituting another sugar. The recipe is fairly flexible. For the milk, I like using whole milk for flavor, but you can use a nondairy milk or even just water. Please know that the less fat that is in your milk, the less flexible your mochi will be after it has cooled down. So if you really want a very soft and stretchy mochi even after your pies have been baked and cooled, I recommend a milk with a higher fat content.

Pie Crust and Pumpkin Butter

I have not yet ventured into the territory of making my own pumpkin butter, and that’s okay. Because Trader Joe’s makes a delicious one. That’s the one I used for this recipe, if you’d like to keep things exactly the same as what you see in the photos. The sprinkles are also from Trader Joe’s. Did you know their sprinkles don’t use any artificial dyes? Thank goodness, because my kids eat them by the fistful.

As for the pie crust, I also bought mine from Trader Joe’s. For you overachievers, you absolutely can make your own from scratch. I actually do sometimes make a pie crust – I happen to like the one I use for my Maui manju.

Also: feel free to substitute the pumpkin butter for other spreads! The Trader Joe’s apple pie spread is another one of my favorites.

The Icing

Let’s be honest, when we make hand pies, we really just want homemade Pop-Tarts, right? And it wouldn’t be a Pop-Tart without icing on top. Icing is so so so easy to make. Just mix 1/4 cup of the powdered sugar with 1 tbsp of the pumpkin butter. It’s going to seem too thick and dry at first but KEEP MIXING. If it’s been a couple minutes and the sugar is still dry and powdery, then you can add more pumpkin butter a teaspoon at a time. But I find that the most common mistake with icing is adding too much liquid too soon and the icing becomes too thin, dripping off the pie crust. Thicker is better, friends.

Those are all the tips I have for you! This recipe is fairly simple and forgiving. If issues come up, please leave me your questions in the comments below.

Pumpkin Mochi Hand Pie

Mochi Mommy
Inspired by McDonald's Japan, these pumpkin hand pies have a surprise chewy layer of mochi inside.
Servings: 6 pies
Prep Time: 20 minutes mins
Cook Time: 22 minutes mins
Total Time: 42 minutes mins
Print Recipe Pin Recipe Leave a Review

Ingredients
  

Microwave Milk Mochi

  • 1/4 cup mochiko, (about 50g)
  • 1 tbsp sugar
  • 1/2 cup whole milk

Hand Pies

  • 1 store-bought premade pie crust dough
  • 6 tsp pumpkin butter

Icing

  • 1/4 cup powdered sugar, (25g)
  • 1 tbsp pumpkin butter
  • sprinkles, optional

Instructions
 

  • Make the milk mochi: Mix all ingredients for the mochi in a microwave safe dish. Cover and microwave for 2 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds. Set aside, covered, while you prepare the hand pies.
  • Preheat oven to 400F and prepare a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  • Make the hand pies: Roll out the pie crust into a 12" square. Slice into 3 rows and 4 columns (or vice versa) for 12 rectangles.
  • Divide your milk mochi into six portions. Dollop one portion of mochi onto the center of a pie crust rectangle. You can spread the mochi out slightly but leave space at the edges of the crust.
  • Add about a teaspoon of pumpkin butter on top of the mochi.
  • Layer another rectangle of pie crust on top. Seal the edges of the hand pie by crimping with a fork. Poke a hole in the center of the pie to let out the steam as it bakes. Repeat with your remaining ingredients until you have six hand pies ready to bake.
  • Bake the hand pies for 20 minutes or until the crust turns a golden brown. Allow pies to cool slightly before frosting.
  • Make the icing: Stir powdered sugar with pumpkin butter. At first it will look too dry but just keep stirring until you get a thick paste-like texture.
  • Spread icing evenly among the six hand pies. Top with sprinkles if you wish. Leftovers can keep in an airtight container in the fridge and can be reheated in the toaster oven or microwave.
